candidates.title: Preassemble an ER32 collet into its eccentric clamping nut
candidates.objective: Orient a matching ER32 collet and clamping nut, place the collet extraction groove into the eccentric ring at the nut’s marked point, then tilt and roll the collet until it audibly and mechanically seats. Stop before tool insertion, threading onto a holder, or torque tightening.
candidates.success_conditions: The correct collet is retained continuously around the nut’s eccentric ring after both grippers release it for 3 seconds, and a light nondestructive withdrawal check does not separate it. The mark and initial groove entry must be used, with no direct axial forcing. Zero score for an unretained or inverted collet, substituting a scripted latch, threading the nut onto a holder before verified engagement, permanent collet deformation, nut damage, dropped parts, or teleport/state overwrite. Partial credit may recognize correct orientation and initial groove capture, but not false retention.
candidates.industrial_value: REGO-FIX specifies nut-collet preassembly as a required tooling-system step and warns that improper assembly can damage collet concentricity or destroy the nut. Hiteco documents industrial MTC electrospindles using ER32 tooling, supporting relevance to robot-associated machining equipment without claiming that arbitrary manufacturers’ internal retention geometries are interchangeable.
candidates.dexterity: High. The defining motion is a constrained eccentric-lip capture followed by a changing-axis tilt/roll and snap engagement, not connector mating or ordinary peg insertion.

candidates.asset_plan: Do not build from nominal ER32 envelope dimensions alone. Acquire one mutually compatible physical REGO-FIX ER32 collet/nut pair or manufacturer-authorized internal CAD, measure the marked eccentric ring, extraction groove, lip eccentricity, lead-in, and elastic deflection, and record provenance. First test whether the pinned Isaac Sim 6.1 rigid-contact model can reproduce correct marked-point entry, snap retention, wrong-angle rejection, removal resistance, and reset repeatability. If essential collet spring deformation cannot be reproduced without an already validated compliant model, reject the task rather than using a magic latch. YAM reach and fingertip clearance must be checked at full scale before demo work.
candidates.risk: Blocked, not selected. The acquired sources prove the sequence and consequence but do not expose the internal eccentric-lip geometry, permissible deformation, snap force, or a licensed downloadable ER32 nut/collet asset. The available Hiteco dimensions establish ER32 industrial equipment, not interchangeability with REGO-FIX retention geometry. Existing novelty records include unrelated push-fit-collet release tasks; this assembly objective appears mechanically distinct, but a complete synchronized submission review remains required.

candidates.title: Align AZ-100 end-of-arm tooling to the mold centerline and lock the adjustment
candidates.objective: On a de-energized AZ-100 vertical-position adjustment fixture, loosen the adjusting-screw jam nut and both clamp bolts, rotate the adjusting screw until the end-of-arm-tooling datum coincides with the specified mold centerline, tighten both clamp bolts while preserving alignment, and finally tighten the jam nut without shifting the setting.
candidates.success_conditions: After release and a 3-second hold, the tooling datum remains within a preregistered measurement tolerance derived from reference hardware of the mold-centerline target; both clamp bolts and the jam nut are restored to hardware-measured service torque windows; and the adjustment has not been used to limit cylinder stroke. Zero score for tightening clamps before alignment, leaving any lock loose, moving a proximity-switch actuator clamp as a shortcut, damaging threads or guide tubes, energizing the fixture, dropping a tool, or teleport/state overwrite. Partial credit may distinguish safe unlock, correct adjustment direction, achieved alignment before locking, and retained alignment after locking.
candidates.industrial_value: The manufacturer defines this operation specifically as alignment of end-of-arm tooling to a mold centerline and warns that using the proximity-switch actuator clamp instead can damage robot components. It is therefore a robot setup operation whose quality directly affects the tooling-to-process interface.
candidates.dexterity: High but rigid-body feasible. The robot must sequence a jam nut, paired clamp bolts, and a screw-driven alignment, then manage tightening reaction without losing the calibrated position. That tests preservation of an adjusted state under later fastening forces rather than generic nut tightening.

candidates.asset_plan: Create a full-scale rigid test fixture only after measuring a matching AZ-100 adjustment assembly or obtaining its applicable drawing: screw pitches, lock-nut and clamp-bolt sizes, clamp compliance, travel, tool access, and fastening torques are absent from the acquired text. Use revolute/prismatic PhysX joints and frictional threaded-drive equivalents whose displacement follows actual screw rotation; never map gripper pose directly to alignment state. Validate unlock dependence, screw direction and pitch, clamp retention, jam-nut reaction, wrong-order controls, overload damage thresholds, and repeated resets before connecting YAM.
candidates.risk: Promising but not selected because the currently acquired manual lacks fastener dimensions, screw pitch, torque specifications for these adjustment fasteners, allowable centerline error, and accessible fixture geometry. Those are mandatory reference-hardware measurements, not values to invent. The operation is semantically different from benchmark knob turning or generic fastening, but full accepted/pending/open/team comparison is still incomplete.

candidates.title: Register and secure an AZ-100 proximity switch beneath its actuator
candidates.objective: With the robot de-energized and its cylinder first retracted, loosen the proximity-switch mount screws, slide the switch beneath the actuator until the indicator changes state while maintaining at most 6 mm sensing clearance and actuator overtravel past switch centerline, then tighten the mount screws without losing registration; repeat for the extended endpoint.
candidates.success_conditions: For both retracted and extended endpoints, robot-applied motions alone place the actuator past the switch centerline, leave the sensing surface no more than 6 mm away, produce the modeled indicator transition only from physical proximity, and retain the switch pose for 3 seconds after mount-screw tightening and tool release. Zero score for adjusting while powered, failing to retract before the first adjustment, registering only one endpoint, relying on indicator state without geometric clearance, actuator collision, loose or stripped screws, moving the actuator instead of the switch, or teleport/state overwrite. Partial credit may recognize safe initial state, correct screw release, one valid endpoint, and retained registration after tightening.
candidates.industrial_value: AAC requires this adjustment after any position adjustment, so it is a recurring calibration step in maintenance of an industrial take-out robot. The manual supplies both the physical registration procedure and a quantitative sensing-clearance limit.
candidates.dexterity: Moderate-to-high and feasible as a rigid PhysX task. It combines partial fastener release, constrained sliding, sensing-state interpretation, sub-centimeter clearance control, holding position against screw-tightening reaction, and repetition at two articulated endpoint configurations.

candidates.asset_plan: Use the official section 4.2.1 arrangement plus measurements from one matching AZ-100 switch, actuator, slot, bracket, and screws. Build the cylinder/actuator and slotted switch mount as rigid articulated bodies at actual scale. Implement indicator state solely as a readout of sensor-actuator distance and relative pose, never as an action-triggered success flag. Before YAM integration, validate screw retention, sliding only when loosened, the 6 mm boundary, over-center criterion, collision rejection, endpoint articulation, tightening drift, reset repeatability, fingertip clearance, and full-scale reach in pinned Isaac Sim 6.1.0/YAM commit 0059d02a1a91bc6834c1d0846022891df0c78730.
candidates.risk: Lowest implementation risk of the three, but still conditional on acquiring matching component geometry, fastener dimensions, and a safe full-scale fixture. The sourced benchmark catalogs contain switch flipping, knob turning, sliders, insertion, latching, and generic fastening, but no objective combining loosen-slide-sense-hold-retighten calibration at two articulated endpoints was found. Cached submission records searched by objective/skill terms revealed no confirmed same task, but that is not proof of complete novelty; synchronized accepted/pending/open/team review is required before construction and again after completion.

selection_reason: This is the only candidate presently supported by a manufacturer procedure, an explicit quantitative geometric criterion, rigid-body physics, and a compact full-scale fixture plausibly reachable by YAM. It tests calibration under fastening reaction rather than a cosmetic variant of switching, sliding, or screw tightening. ER32 preassembly remains blocked by missing eccentric-lip geometry and potentially essential elastic collet deformation; the AZ-100 centerline adjustment is valuable but lacks the dimensions, torque limits, and allowable alignment error needed for a defensible scorer. Selection is conditional rather than a success assertion: reference-component measurement, complete novelty synchronization, rigid environment diagnostics, and YAM reach/force tests must pass before full demo development.
